Title: Optional wolfSSL crypto example would statically link GPL code into the firmware
Impact: In the default build: no exposure. With the crypto example on under the GPL option, distributing the firmware would mean offering the complete corresponding source of the whole image (MITRE code, MSDK and wolfSSL) under GPL-3.0. On a device that only boots signed or packaged images, GPL-3.0 section 6 also requires the Installation Information needed to install modified firmware. Either of these would make this a Red.
Recommendation: Decide this now and record it. Either (a) keep CRYPTO_EXAMPLE=0 and enforce it, for example a CI check that fails if decoder/wolfssl/ exists or CRYPTO_EXAMPLE=1 in a release build; or (b) buy a wolfSSL commercial licence before enabling it; or (c) use a permissive crypto library instead, such as Mbed TLS / TF-PSA-Crypto (Apache-2.0), Monocypher (BSD-2-Clause or CC0) or tinycrypt (BSD-3-Clause), or the MAX78000's hardware AES/TRNG drivers from the MSDK.
References: GPL-3.0 §5(c) whole work; GPL-3.0 §6 Installation Information (User Products); wolfSSL dual licensing (GPL / commercial)

Title: ADI MSDK v2024_02 is linked into the firmware but downloaded at build time and not scanned
Impact: The largest third-party part of the shipped image has unconfirmed licences and attributions. If any linked MSDK file is under a more restrictive or vendor-only licence, that is not known. Apache-2.0 §4 notice obligations for the MSDK are not being met at the moment (see OSS-003).
Recommendation: Run ScanCode over msdk-2024_02/Libraries (at least CMSIS/Device/Maxim/MAX78000, PeriphDrivers and Boards/MAX78000/FTHR_RevA) together with a linker map from 'make release' (pass it with --map), then update confirmed_components.json with the concluded licences and licence-file paths and regenerate the notices and SBOM. Record any ADI use-restriction text from the MSDK licence files.
References: Apache-2.0 §4; ADI MSDK licence files (to be confirmed)

Title: 'Educational purposes only' wording in every source header sits beside the Apache-2.0 grant
Impact: For the eCTF competition itself: none. For anyone reusing this code in a commercial product: an unresolved question about whether non-educational use is permitted. That needs a recorded position before the code ships outside the competition.
Recommendation: If you reuse this code commercially, record a position from legal, ideally backed by written confirmation from MITRE that Apache-2.0 governs and the header text is a disclaimer. If you maintain a fork, add 'SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0' to each first-party file so the grant sits next to the wording.

Title: No third-party notices ship with the firmware binary
Impact: Distributing the binary without these notices does not meet Apache-2.0 §4(a) (give recipients a copy of the licence), the Maxim licence condition (the copyright notice and permission notice must be included in all copies or substantial portions) or newlib's BSD-style attribution conditions. This is easy to fix, but it is an obligation.
Recommendation: Review and complete the generated draft THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md: add the MSDK, newlib and libgcc licence texts it marks as missing, and cut the Maxim entry down to its licence header. Ship it with every firmware release (release bundle, product documentation or a support web page).
References: Apache-2.0 §4(a), §4(c); Maxim Integrated MIT-style licence (notice condition); newlib COPYING.NEWLIB

Title: No SBOM, and the build pulls the SDK and base image by mutable reference
Impact: Release-by-release notices and SBOMs cannot be shown to be accurate. Under the EU Cyber Resilience Act, a manufacturer placing a product like this on the EU market must keep an SBOM of at least its top-level dependencies.
Recommendation: Pin the base image by digest and the apt toolchain packages by version, verify the MSDK zip against a recorded SHA-256, and add a lockfile (pip-tools or uv) for the host packages. Regenerate sbom.cdx.json for each release from a linker map and a confirmed component list; the draft produced by this review is a starting point.
References: EU CRA Annex I Part II (1) SBOM; CycloneDX 1.5

Title: Build container toolchain is GPL but build-only; linked runtime is covered by exceptions
Impact: No copyleft obligation on the firmware from the toolchain, provided the build container itself is not handed to customers or contract manufacturers. If it is, that is distribution of GPL programs, and the source-offer obligations apply.
Recommendation: No change needed. Add the newlib and libgcc licence texts to the notices (OSS-003). If the Docker image is ever given to third parties, provide the Ubuntu source packages or a written offer.
References: GCC Runtime Library Exception 3.1; newlib COPYING.NEWLIB

Title: Host Python dependencies are permissive or file-level copyleft and stay internal
Impact: None while the tooling stays internal. If design/ or tools/ is ever given to customers or a factory, tqdm's MPL-2.0 files need source availability for any modifications (none are made), and every package needs its notice.
Recommendation: Run 'pip-licenses --with-license-file' in the installed venv to confirm, and pin versions in a lockfile (OSS-005). Re-rate if the host tooling becomes a deliverable.

Title: Maxim startup file flagged 'proprietary' by ScanCode is a permissive MIT-style licence
Impact: No distribution blocker. The only obligation is to keep the Maxim copyright and permission notice with the firmware (covered by OSS-003) and not use Maxim's name beyond what its branding policy allows.
Recommendation: Record the concluded licence (MIT-style with Maxim branding and IP clauses) in the component list, as done in confirmed_components.json, so future scans don't escalate it. Keep the headers intact in any fork.
References: MIT; ScanCode known false positive: 'All Rights Reserved' / IP-retention clause in permissive text

Title: First-party files and Python packages don't declare their licence
Impact: Hygiene only. Scanners and downstream SBOM tools report these packages as having no licence data, and files copied out of the repository lose their licence context.
Recommendation: Add 'SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0' to first-party headers, and 'license = "Apache-2.0"' plus 'license-files = ["LICENSE.txt"]' to both pyproject.toml files.
